headings.text: What actually matters in a water purifier under Rs 25,000

cta.headline: Want the full spreadsheet?
cta.sub: Compare 25+ RO+UV purifiers side-by-side -- TDS handling, tank size, filter cost, real user complaints.

faq.q: Is a Rs 20,000 water purifier really better than a Rs 10,000 one?
faq.a: Yes, in three measurable ways: TDS adjustment (mineralizer adds back calcium and magnesium that RO strips out), filter life (premium filters last 12 months vs 6 on budget models), and tank build quality (food-grade steel vs plastic on cheap units). The cheap ones work, but taste flatter and filter replacements add up faster.

faq.q: Do I need UV if I have RO?
faq.a: For municipal tap water in Indian metros, RO alone is sufficient. UV adds protection against bacteria and viruses in case the RO membrane is aging or feed water is contaminated. For borewell water or tanker-supplied water, both RO and UV are essential.

faq.q: How much do water purifier filters cost annually?
faq.a: Budget purifiers cost Rs 1,500-2,500 per year in filters. Premium purifiers like the picks below average Rs 1,800-2,200 per year -- similar total cost but with better membrane life. The Aquaguard and Pureit service networks include filter cost in annual maintenance contracts (AMC) for Rs 2,500-4,000 per year.

faq.q: What TDS level is safe to drink after RO?
faq.a: RO strips TDS down to 30-50 ppm, which is too low for taste and health (the WHO recommends 100-300 ppm). Premium purifiers add a mineralizer stage to bring TDS back to 150-200 ppm. If you drink RO water straight, add a pinch of pink salt or use a mineralizer cartridge.

faq.q: Can a water purifier work without electricity?
faq.a: No. RO+UV purifiers need power to run the pump and UV lamp. The picks below all have built-in tanks so you can still drink during power cuts (6-12 hours of storage). For areas with frequent long outages, consider a non-electric gravity-based purifier as a backup.

meta.tldr_pick: The Eureka Forbes Aquaguard Aura RO+UV+MTDS is the best water purifier under Rs 25,000 for most Indian homes -- 7-litre tank, mineralizer stage that adds back calcium and magnesium, and the widest service network in India. Runners-up are the Pureit Ultima for smaller families and the Kent Grand Plus for tech-forward users who want app connectivity.
key_takeaways: Mineralizer stage matters: pure RO water strips beneficial minerals and tastes flat -- spend the money on a purifier that adds them back.
Skip the Livpure Glo Pro: Rs 18,000 for a 5-litre tank with no mineralizer and slow refill rate -- the Aquaguard Aura is the same price with a 7L tank and TDS controller.
Service network beats specs on paper: Aquaguard has 600+ service centres across India, Kent has 250+, Pureit has 200+. Filter replacement turnaround time matters more than initial price.
7-litre tank is the sweet spot for a family of 4: smaller tanks need frequent refills, larger tanks waste energy keeping water cool.
meta.who_for: Indian families in metros and tier-2 cities who use municipal tap water with TDS between 200-1500 ppm, want RO+UV protection, and need a service-backed purifier that survives 5+ years of use.
meta.methodology: We compared 5 RO+UV water purifiers under Rs 25,000 available on Amazon India and Flipkart in September 2026. For each, we evaluated TDS handling (with and without mineralizer), tank size, filter life, service network coverage, and 90-day user review patterns. Picks were cross-checked against Eureka Forbes, HUL Pureit, and Kent annual maintenance contracts to surface total ownership cost.

body:
What actually matters in a water purifier under Rs 25,000

Skip the marketing. Three specs decide if a water purifier is worth buying: RO+UV+MTDS stage count, tank size (7L for a family of 4), and service network coverage. Everything else -- copper cartridges, alkaline stages, app connectivity -- is incremental improvement that matters less than the basics working reliably.

The Rs 12,000-25,000 bracket is where Indian purifier brands make their money, and the competition in 2026 is fierce. Eureka Forbes (Aquaguard), HUL (Pureit), Kent, and Blue Star are the established players; Livpure and A.O. Smith compete aggressively on price. We compared five current models for this guide, weighing TDS handling with and without mineralizer stages, tank size for typical family use, filter replacement cost, and the practical reality of service network turnaround time.

What most buyers underestimate: the cost of filter replacements adds Rs 2,500-4,000 per year on top of the initial price. Purifiers with annual maintenance contracts (AMC) often work out cheaper than pay-as-you-go, and the brands with the widest service networks can usually send a technician within 24-48 hours -- critical when your only source of drinking water is a purifier that stops working on a Sunday night.

One more consideration for Indian homes: input water TDS. Municipal water in metros is usually 200-500 ppm (TDS below 200 needs only UV, not RO; TDS above 1,500 from borewell needs a more aggressive membrane). The picks below assume municipal supply in the 200-800 ppm range -- which covers 80%+ of Indian households.

If you only buy one thing from this list: get the Eureka Forbes Aquaguard Aura RO+UV+MTDS at Rs 23,990. 7-litre tank, mineralizer stage for taste, and Aquaguard has 600+ service centres across India -- the widest network of any purifier brand. If the filter ever fails, a technician is on your doorstep within 24 hours.

Our top 4 picks

🏅 Top Pick

1. Eureka Forbes Aquaguard Aura RO+UV+MTDS

₹23,990
TechnologyRO+UV+MTDS
Tank Size7L
Filter Life12 months
Service Network600+ centres

The Aquaguard Aura is the best overall pick for a 4-person Indian family. The MTDS (Mineral Taste Booster) stage is the differentiator -- it adds calcium and magnesium back into the RO-purified water, which fixes the flat taste that turns people off from RO purifiers. The 7-litre tank is large enough for 4 people to drink, cook, and refill bottles without running dry mid-day. Aquaguard has 600+ service centres across India -- if your filter dies on a weekend, a technician is usually at your door within 24 hours.

Pros

  • MTDS mineralizer -- fixes the flat RO taste
  • 7L tank is the right size for 4-person family
  • 600+ service centres -- widest network in India
  • 12-month filter life

Cons

  • No app or smart connectivity
  • Annual AMC is Rs 3,500 (above average)
  • Plastic body, not metal
🏅 Runner-up

2. Pureit Ultima RO+UV (HUL)

₹22,500
TechnologyRO+UV+MF
Tank Size6L
Filter Life12 months
Service Network200+ centres

Pureit Ultima is the HUL (Hindustan Unilever) answer to Aquaguard. The 6-litre tank is enough for a family of 3-4, and the MF (microfiltration) stage adds a final polish to the water after RO+UV. Pureit service is solid but the network is smaller than Aquaguard -- turnaround times in tier-2 cities can stretch to 3-4 days. If you already have HUL service in your area (most metros do), the Pureit is a strong runner-up.

Pros

  • Trusted HUL brand with stable service
  • Microfiltration stage -- extra polish on output water
  • Pureit AMC is Rs 2,500 (cheapest in this bracket)
  • Lower initial price than Aquaguard

Cons

  • 6L tank is smaller than ideal for 4-person family
  • No mineralizer stage (taste is flatter than Aquaguard)
  • 200+ service centres vs 600+ for Aquaguard
💰 Tech Pick

3. Kent Grand Plus RO+UV+UF (TDS Controller)

₹24,500
TechnologyRO+UV+UF
Tank Size8L
Filter Life12 months
Service Network250+ centres

The Kent Grand Plus wins on tank size and tech. The 8-litre tank is the largest in this bracket, which makes it the best pick for families of 5 or for homes where the purifier also feeds an RO-based geyser or dishwasher. The TDS controller lets you dial in the desired mineral level, which is great if your input water TDS varies seasonally. App connectivity is a nice-to-have, not a must-have.

Pros

  • 8L tank -- largest in the bracket
  • Adjustable TDS controller
  • App connectivity for filter alerts
  • Computer-controlled purification process

Cons

  • Most expensive in this roundup at Rs 24,500
  • 8L tank wastes energy if you are a 2-person household
  • Kent AMC is Rs 4,000 (the highest)

4. Blue Star Aristo RO+UV+UF

₹21,990
TechnologyRO+UV+UF
Tank Size7L
Filter Life12 months
Service Network150+ centres

The Blue Star Aristo is the value pick in this bracket. At Rs 21,990 it undercuts Aquaguard by Rs 2,000 and Pureit by Rs 500, while offering the same 7-litre tank and 12-month filter life. Blue Star is best known for air conditioners, but their water purifier build quality matches Aquaguard and Kent. Service network is smaller (150+ centres) -- if you live in a tier-2 city, check availability first.

Pros

  • Lowest price in the roundup at Rs 21,990
  • 7L tank matches the Aquaguard
  • Solid build quality from Blue Star
  • 12-month filter life

Cons

  • No mineralizer stage (water tastes flatter)
  • 150+ service centres is the smallest in the bracket
  • Smaller tank for hot Indian summers can run dry

The one we recommend skipping

⚠️ Skip

Livpure Glo Pro RO+UV

₹17,990
TechnologyRO+UV
Tank Size5L
Filter Life6 months
Service Network100+ centres

The Livpure Glo Pro looks tempting at Rs 17,990 -- Rs 6,000 cheaper than the Aquaguard -- but the savings disappear quickly. The 5-litre tank is too small for a 4-person Indian family (refills every 6-8 hours during summer), the 6-month filter life doubles your annual filter cost, and the 100+ service centre network means 4-7 day turnaround in tier-2 cities. No mineralizer stage means flat-tasting water. Spend the extra Rs 6,000 on the Aquaguard Aura and get a 7L tank, 12-month filters, mineralizer stage, and a service network 6x larger. The Livpure is fine for a single-person household, not a family.

Frequently asked questions

Is a Rs 20,000 water purifier really better than a Rs 10,000 one?

Yes, in three measurable ways: TDS adjustment (mineralizer adds back calcium and magnesium that RO strips out), filter life (premium filters last 12 months vs 6 on budget models), and tank build quality (food-grade steel vs plastic on cheap units). The bottom line

The sub-Rs 25,000 water purifier market in India is mature and competitive in 2026. The Eureka Forbes Aquaguard Aura RO+UV+MTDS at Rs 23,990 is the best pick for most families -- MTDS mineralizer fixes the flat RO taste, the 7-litre tank handles a family of 4, and Aquaguard has the widest service network in India (600+ centres).

Families who want HUL-grade reliability should pick the Pureit Ultima at Rs 22,500 (cheapest AMC). Larger families of 5+ should pick the Kent Grand Plus at Rs 24,500 for the 8L tank and TDS controller. And value buyers who want the same 7L tank as Aquaguard for less should pick the Blue Star Aristo at Rs 21,990.

Skip the Livpure Glo Pro -- the Rs 6,000 savings evaporate once you factor in the smaller tank, shorter filter life, smaller service network, and absent mineralizer stage.

Two ownership tips that keep a water purifier healthy: replace the sediment and carbon filters every 6 months even if the purifier says they are fine (the saturation is gradual and you will not notice the drop until year 2), and clean the storage tank every 6 months by emptying it, refilling with clean water, and discarding the first 2 litres after refill. With those two habits, any of the four picks above should serve 5-7 years.
